questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Italy and its rich culture. I also appreciate Milan's transportation network, which makes it easy and convenient to travel to many different destinations across the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not that difficult. However, the overall approach at the university was quite relaxed and less structured than I am used to, which could create a lot of uncertainty. Fortunately, there were many Danish students, and we supported and helped each other with information etc. through the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We attended an Erasmus orientation presentation, and during our visit to the Mobility Office, we were given an introduction to the course and exam registration process, including how and when to register.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I recommend getting in contact with former Erasmus students, as they can provide valuable advice and share contact information for potential landlords.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The standard of cleanliness and tidiness was generally lower than what I was accustomed to in Denmark.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, the course registration process was quite unstructured. However, since there were many law students participating in the exchange programme, we were able to share information with each other throughout the process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
At the beginning of the semester, you have the opportunity to attend different courses before deciding which ones to enrol in. There is no fixed deadline for choosing your courses, as the process may vary depending on the professor.

Once you have decided which courses you would like to take, you register for them through the Unimia website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contact either the course professor or the designated contact person at the University of Milan.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the courses I wanted to attend.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend attending a variety of courses at the beginning of the semester, as I found that the teaching style and approach of the professor had a significant influence on my overall course experience and choice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, I found that the academic level of the courses was lower than that at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Milan, the teaching was primarily based on PowerPoint presentations and lectures. In some courses, students were also required to prepare a presentation or complete a midterm assessment, both of which formed part of the final course evaluation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Contract Law
Cultural Diversity and Human Rights Law
Gender Justice
Public and Private Partnership for Sustainable Development 
International Criminal Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I particularly enjoyed the course Public and Private Partnership for Sustainable Development, mainly because of the professor. I also appreciated the assessment format, as the exam was relatively relaxed.

I also found Comparative Contract Law to be quite manageable, as the assessment consisted of a multiple-choice examination.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation in Milan is relatively inexpensive, and it is possible to purchase a monthly travel pass. However, I mostly walked around the city and therefore did not find it necessary to buy one.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the time to explore the different neighbourhoods of Milan and enjoy everything the city has to offer. I would also highly recommend travelling to other parts of Italy, for example by taking day trips to Bologna or Verona.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Approach the local students that are attending the same courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The aperitivo which was such a vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Although the Italian university system may seem unstructured at times, everything usually works out in the end. My advice is to stay patient, be flexible, and not worry too much if the process initially feels unclear.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The examination format is not always fixed and may change during the semester, sometimes even shortly before the final examination. This depends on the professor.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The other Danish students I met during my exchange experience, as well as the Italian culture and the atmosphere in Milan in general, made the experience truly amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: N/A

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
